verdict.rationale: Keycloak is itself a standards-based OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect authorization server. Developers register clients, including through a dynamic client registration endpoint, and Keycloak issues tokens to them. It also publishes a well-known discovery document, supports token introspection and revocation, client credentials and device grants, and offers themes so the login page can carry your app's branding. Community users confirm running it in production as the OIDC provider for many apps. Missing for 10: no evidence of a user consent screen or third-party-client controls (distinguishing first-party from external clients), and no explicit authorization-code/authorize endpoint documentation in the pack; it also runs as a separate server rather than embedding into the developer's own app.
